comparisons.peer_summary: Sales are primarily made via purchase orders or agreements, but these do not necessarily indicate future sales as they may be revised or canceled without penalty.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AMD disclose that their sales are primarily conducted via purchase orders, which introduce visibility but also cancellation or revision risks. QCOM specifically notes the ability for customers to reschedule or cancel orders prior to shipment, while AMD highlights that such orders may be revised or canceled without penalty and may not indicate actual future sales.

sentences.text: QCT's sales are primarily made through supply terms which implement a purchase order and order confirmation process for delivery of products.

QCT generally allows customers to reschedule delivery dates within a defined time frame and to cancel orders prior to shipment with or without payment of a cancellation fee, depending on when the order is canceled.
Sales are made primarily pursuant to purchase orders for current delivery or agreements covering purchases over a period of time.

Although such orders or agreements may provide visibility into future quarters, they may not necessarily be indicative of actual sales for any succeeding period as some of these orders or agreements may be revised or canceled without penalty.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD markets products through direct and co-marketing programs, including cooperative advertising with customers and third parties where market development funds may be provided for eligible customers to reimburse for advertisements related to AMD and third-party systems.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies utilize co-marketing programs and partnerships to promote their brands. QCOM markets through direct efforts, partnerships, and collaborations to expand brand awareness, while AMD markets through direct and co-marketing programs, including cooperative advertising where customers may receive funds for advertisements related to their products.

sentences.text: Through direct marketing efforts, partnerships and collaborations (including marketing programs with customers), products powered by Snapdragon and Qualcomm technologies are marketed to expand the reach of both brands to drive awareness and preference.
We market our products through direct marketing and co-marketing programs.

In addition, we have cooperative advertising and marketing programs with customers and third parties, including market development programs, pursuant to which we may provide product information, training, marketing materials and funds.

comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom sells products via direct sales force, distributors, and channel partners, with distributors and OEMs/contract manufacturers accounting for the substantial majority of semiconductor sales. The company utilizes a mix of large global distributors, regional distributors, and direct relationships with OEMs, supported by specialized sales forces and logistics infrastructure.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and Broadcom sell through a combination of direct sales forces and channel partners/distributors. QCOM relies on supply terms with purchase orders for delivery, while Broadcom explicitly states it sells via direct sales force and a select network of distributors, with distributors and OEMs/contract manufacturers accounting for the substantial majority of semiconductor sales.

We sell our products through our direct sales force and a select network of distributors and channel partners globally.
Distributors and OEMs, or their contract manufacturers, typically account for the substantial majority of our semiconductor sales.

comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and Intel maintain cooperative advertising or marketing programs with customers to promote their brands. QCOM mentions marketing programs with customers as part of its direct marketing efforts, while Intel explicitly states it maintains cooperative advertising programs with customers to promote its brands and identify genuine components.
